name: Barbell Drag Curl
description: The drag curl is a barbell curl variation where the bar is dragged upward along the torso rather than curled forward in a standard arc. By pulling the elbows back as the bar rises, the biceps are placed under a unique tension angle and the brachialis is recruited heavily. The dragging path also eliminates front deltoid assistance, making it a stricter bicep isolation exercise than the standard curl.

execution.starting_position: Stand upright holding a barbell at arm's length in a supinated grip. Bar rests at thigh level.
execution.setup_instructions: Use a straight barbell or EZ-bar. Grip shoulder-width. Stand tall.
steps: Step 1: Begin curling by pulling the elbows back and dragging the barbell upward along the torso.
Step 2: The bar should stay close to the body — almost touching — as it travels from thighs to upper abs.
Step 3: Continue until maximum elbow flexion is reached and the bar is near the upper chest.
Step 4: Lower the bar slowly back to the thighs along the same dragging path.
execution.breathing_instructions: Exhale on the curl, inhale on the return.
common_mistakes: Swinging the bar forward instead of dragging it up the body
safety_considerations: Keep the lower back neutral — do not hyperextend to assist the curl
execution.range_of_motion_guidance: Thighs to upper chest, bar stays in contact or near contact with the torso throughout.
coaching_cues: Drag the bar up your shirt
Elbows pull back as the bar rises
